Dog food myths from someone who’s actual job is to read a lot of dog food science.  AS ALWAYS - if you, your dog, your wallet and your vet are happy with your dogs diet please carry on with exactly what makes you happy. These are my evidence backed, thoroughly researched points but I do not know your actual dog or your circumstances ❤️ “Natural is best” - ingredient quality IS important and something to prioritise, but there are things that are more important, like having a complete and balanced diet.  Dogs diverged from wolves tens of thousands of years ago with genes for digesting starch (AMY2B) that wolves don’t have. Different animal, different diet. This does NOT mean I promote feeding dogs high quantities of starches or carbohydrates, or that I don’t prioritise a nutrient dense diet. It just means your dogs diet should be species appropriate.  “If I can’t pronounce it, it’s bad” is a really quick way to deprive your dog from a lot of nutrients. Yes, I’d like my dog to get the vast majority of their nutrients naturally from whole foods BUT there are excellent quality products can contain ingredients that are hard to pronounce.  “High heat destroys the goodness” - extrusion moves the nutrient profile both ways, and proper, respectable diets are formulated around it. Make sure your food is labelled complete and is regularly independently tested.  “Lab-made additives aren’t absorbed” - bioavailability depends on the nutrient’s form, the food matrix, the dose and the individual dog. In some cases natural is best, in some cases it isn’t. I’d rather a dog got fed a lab made vitamin than lacked that vitamin entirely.  “Human-grade is better” - what counts is bioavailability, and whether a diet is complete, balanced, right for life stage and fed in the right amount. Every claim here is anchored to peer-reviewed research and veterinary nutrition textbooks. Sources in the comments if you want them. I’m a canine nutritionist (which means my job is to study dog food science) and I am not a vet - please please please contact them for any worries or questions you may have about your dogs health.  #dogdiet #dogfood #dognutrition #dogfoodreview #kibble
